Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

Title: HHS Approval of Entities That Certify Medical Review Officers
Action: Notice.
Abstract: This notice publishes a list of HHS approved Medical Review Officers (MROs) certification entities. The most recent HHS Mandatory Guidelines for Federal Workplace Drug Testing Programs (Mandatory Guidelines), effective on October 10, 2023, (Oral Fluid) and February 1, 2024, (Urine), address the role and qualifications of MROs and HHS approval of entities that certify MROs.

[2026-21672] Notice — Health and Human Services Department; Health Resources and Services Administration
Title: National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program; List of Petitions Received
Action: Notice.
Abstract: HRSA is publishing this notice of petitions received under the National Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (the Program), as required by the Public Health Service (PHS) Act, as amended. While the Secretary of HHS is named as the respondent in all proceedings brought by the filing of petitions for compensation under the Program, the United States Court of Federal Claims is charged by statute with responsibility for considering and acting upon the petitions.

[2026-21673] Notice — Health and Human Services Department; Health Resources and Services Administration
Title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Submission to OMB for Review and Approval; Public Comment Request: National Practitioner Data Bank for Adverse Information on Physicians and Other Health Care Practitioners-45 CFR Part 60 Regulations and Forms, OMB No. 0906-0081-Revision
Action: Notice.
Abstract: In compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, HRSA submitted an Information Collection Request (ICR) to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval. Comments submitted during the first public review of this ICR will be provided to OMB. OMB will accept further comments from the public during the review and approval period. OMB may act on HRSA's ICR only after the 30-day comment period for this notice has closed.

[2026-21679] Notice — Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
Title: Questions and Answers Regarding Mandatory Cosmetics Recalls; Guidance for Industry; Availability
Action: Notice of availability.
Abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance entitled "Questions and Answers Regarding Mandatory Cosmetics Recalls: Guidance for Industry." The guidance document provides answers to common questions that might arise about FDA's mandatory recall authority for cosmetics. It is intended to inform regulated industry about the Agency's current thinking on implementation of certain aspects, including the criteria, process, and expectations, for mandatory recalls of cosmetic products. The guidance announced in this notice finalizes the draft guidance of the same title published on December 18, 2025.

[2026-21681] Notice — Homeland Security Department; U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement
Title: Agency Information Collection Activities: Allegation of Counterfeiting and Intellectual Policy, ICE Form 73-048, OMB 1653-0053
Action: 60-Day Notice and request for comments.
Abstract: The Department of Homeland Security will submit the following Information Collection Request (ICR) to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and clearance in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.

[2026-21685] Notice — Justice Department; Education Department
Title: Clarification on Department of Justice and Department of Education Guidance Documents Regarding Federal Nondiscrimination Laws
Action: Notice; clarification.
Abstract: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) and U.S. Department of Education (ED) (the Departments) are issuing this document to clarify that seven guidance documents issued jointly by the Departments are not enforceable. In addition, the Departments plan to revisit these guidance documents in light of the Supreme Court's decision in Loper Bright Enters. v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369, 400 (2024), to assess whether they are consistent with the single best meaning of the relevant statutory text. The Departments will not rely upon these guidance documents in their enforcement of federal civil rights laws, including Titles IV and VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title IV and Title VI), 42 U.S.C. 2000c et seq. and 2000d et seq., the Equal Educational Opportunities Act of 1974 (EEOA), 20 U.S.C. 1701-1720, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA), 42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq., and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (Section 504), 29 U.S.C. 794.

Action: Notice of Department of State Sanctions Actions Pursuant to the Executive Order Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court.
Abstract: The Department of State is publishing the names of one or more persons that have been placed on the Department of the Treasury's List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List) administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

[2026-21712] Notice — Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
Title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission for Office of Management and Budget Review; Comment Request; Accreditation Scheme for Conformity Assessment Program
Action: Notice.
Abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is announcing that a proposed collection of information has been submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and clearance under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.

[2026-21713] Notice — Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
Title: Agency Information Collection Activities; Proposed Collection; Comment Request; Product Jurisdiction and Combination Products
Action: Notice.
Abstract: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing an opportunity for public comment on the proposed collection of certain information by the Agency. Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), Federal Agencies are required to publish notice in the Federal Register concerning each proposed collection of information, including each proposed extension of an existing collection of information, and to allow 60 days for public comment in response to the notice. This notice solicits comments on information collection associated with product jurisdiction and combination product regulations.

Company: CornerCare Pharmacy

US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

Rules that APPLY:
- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming
